ideas.description: Replace the no-op baseline in submissions/arena/ with the futurebiohackers airbench96-style recipe as published (A1a): frozen 2x2 patch-whitening stem, 3-conv groups at widths 128/384/576, SGD-Nesterov lr 9 with BN biases at 64x LR, label smoothing 0.3, lookahead-EMA, alternating flip + translate 2, 8.5 epochs, bs 1024, fp16 + channels_last, GPU-resident uint8 data with GPU-side augmentation. In build, run torch.compile max-autotune and warm it up on synthetic inputs for both train and eval shapes, including eval batch sizes 1..1024 or dynamic, and the cuDNN/CUDA init. E000 showed lazy init landing in the first timed trial. Log the per-trial prepare and train split.
ideas.expected: First feasible run: accuracy ~0.755-0.760 (>=0.753), time ~8-9 s, complete True. All three trial times within ~3% of each other, since warmup moves into build. If accuracy comes in at 0.750-0.753, the next step is the same recipe at 9.0 epochs.

ideas.description: Rerun the A1a reproduction byte-identical, with no code change, to measure run-to-run time and accuracy noise. Record the per-seed accuracy std and the per-trial prepare/train times from both runs.
ideas.expected: Mean accuracy within 0.15 pp of A1a, mean time within 2%, per-seed std <=0.35 pp. This sets the threshold below which later time gains count as noise.

ideas.description: On top of A1a, apply dirac (identity) init to the second and third conv of each group, the parts that map channels to themselves, as in airbench. Cut epochs from 8.5 to 7.5 and change nothing else.
ideas.expected: Accuracy stays >=0.753 (roughly -0.1 to -0.3 pp vs A1a). Time drops ~10-12%, to about 7.5-8 s.

ideas.description: On top of A1a, replace every GELU activation with SiLU (same compile and epochs). If the reference already uses ReLU or SiLU, test GELU->ReLU on whichever activation it does use.
ideas.expected: Time -2 to -4%, accuracy within ±0.2 pp of A1a.

ideas.description: On top of A1a, compute the patch-whitening eigendecomposition on the first 1500 training images instead of 5000, and do normalization in fp16 on the GPU in one fused pass. Instrument prepare time separately.
ideas.expected: Prepare time -30% or more. If prepare is >=3% of the total, total time falls ~1-2%. Accuracy within ±0.2 pp.

ideas.description: On top of A1a, widen the last group from 576 to 768 channels and cut epochs from 8.5 to 7.5. Recompile and warm up the new shapes in build.
ideas.expected: Per-epoch cost +~6-8%, epochs -12%, net time -3 to -5%. Accuracy ~0.754-0.758 (>=0.753).

ideas.description: On top of A1a, train at 24 px for the first ~40% of epochs, 28 px for the next ~30% and 32 px for the rest, with random-resized crops on the GPU. Add +0.5 epochs (9.0 total). Compile and warm up all three shapes in build so no recompile happens in timed code. The final EMA/eval runs at 32 px.
ideas.expected: Time -5 to -10% vs A1a. Accuracy -0.1 to -0.4 pp (risk of dropping below 0.753, explore).

ideas.description: On top of A1a, raise the batch size from 1024 to 2000 at equal epochs. Scale lr, wd and EMA/lookahead intervals by the kilostep rule: keep lr*wd per example, and scale the step-based schedule by the step count. Warm up the new shapes in build.
ideas.expected: Time -3 to -6% from fewer steps and better utilization. Accuracy -0.2 to -0.6 pp (likely near or below threshold, explore).

structured_output.summary:
So far there's only the no-op baseline: accuracy 0.012, time 0.11 s, not feasible. The queue was empty, so I queued 8 ideas and dropped none.

**First run (priority 5):** reproduce the futurebiohackers airbench96-style recipe (A1a) to get the first run that meets the 0.753 accuracy target. All compile and CUDA/cuDNN warmup has to happen in `build`. E000 showed that otherwise lazy CUDA init lands in the first timed trial.

**Next, all built on A1a (priority 4):**
- **Noise check:** rerun A1a unchanged to measure run-to-run time and accuracy variation (H4.1.1). This sets how big a time gain has to be before it counts.
- **Dirac init:** add identity init to the group convs and cut from 8.5 to 7.5 epochs (H1.2.1). Expect about 10% less time.

**Smaller exploit ideas (priority 3):**
- GELU to SiLU swap (H2.2.1).
- Compute the whitening statistics on 1500 images instead of 5000 to shrink `prepare` (H3.2.1).
- Last group widened to 768 at 7.5 epochs (H1.3.1).

**Explore ideas (priority 2):**
- Progressive resizing, 24 → 28 → 32 px (H2.1.1).
- Batch size 2000 with the learning rate rescaled (H3.3.1).

I left out a Muon test (H5) because it's unlikely to cut time. If A1a lands at 0.750–0.753, the fallback is the same recipe at 9.0 epochs.
